title: Aleph Hebrew Letter (א): Vowel Marks
description: Learn the Hebrew letter Aleph (א) and its three vowel marks — Patah, Kamatz Gadol and Hataf Patah — with beginner explanations and interactive practice.

2.label: Patah
2.equivalent: Aleph with a single horizontal vowel mark beneath it.

4.label: Kamatz Gadol
4.equivalent: Aleph with a small T-shaped vowel mark beneath it.

6.label: Hataf Patah
6.equivalent: Aleph with a horizontal vowel mark and two vertical dots beneath it.

blocks.0: Aleph Hebrew Letter (א): Vowel Marks & Practice
blocks.8: With Hataf Patah (אֲ), Aleph is read with a reduced [a] vowel. In Modern Hebrew, it is pronounced [a], the same as Patah and Kamatz Gadol.

theory.heading: Meet Aleph
theory.intro: The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet. Start with the letter, then look at the marks around it.
objectives: Distinguish Patah, Kamatz Gadol and Hataf Patah by their shapes.
Identify these vowel marks in beginner practice questions.

examples.heading: One letter, three vowel marks
examples.intro: Look beneath Aleph. Notice the line, the T-shaped mark, and the line with two dots.
